title: Power Pages: site analytics and server logging configuration
summary: The roadmap details and documented configuration routes check out. The assurance that the feature has no autonomous actions is not established by the sources; smaller corrections should qualify IP-address retention and dashboard coverage, complete the trace-setting path, and cite the Azure billing and access documentation.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, notes, cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Application Insights uses Azure consumption billing for telemetry ingestion, supporting a variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Because workspace-based Application Insights resources store their data in a Log Analytics workspace, the billing for data ingestion and retention is done by the workspace where the Application Insights data is located.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/cost-logs#application-insights-billing to sources for the consumption model and ingestion-volume cost statements.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a Power Pages licence requirement specific to this planned feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages site analytics licensing; Power Pages site analytics Application Insights licensing server logging. Read FAQ and assign-licensing, licensing FAQ and capacity-management excerpts; these describe general site licensing, not a feature-specific entitlement.

claims.claim: No Power Pages-specific charge for this feature has been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages site analytics licensing; Power Pages site analytics Application Insights licensing server logging. Read FAQ and assign-licensing, licensing FAQ and capacity-management excerpts; no separate charge for the planned analytics and logging feature was found.

claims.claim: Application Insights masks stored IP addresses by default.
claims.quote: By default, IP addresses are temporarily collected but not stored. ... The address is then discarded, and 0.0.0.0 is written to the client_IP field.

claims.claim: Retaining IP addresses requires setting the Application Insights component's DisableIpMasking property to true.
claims.quote: To enable IP collection and storage, the DisableIpMasking property of the Application Insights component must be set to true. ... DisableIpMasking applies to classic Application Insights ingestion.
claims.fix: Replace the retaining-addresses clause with: 'For classic Application Insights ingestion, retaining IP addresses requires setting DisableIpMasking to true; native OTLP ingestion does not retain the address regardless of that property.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The exact fields of the planned server and access logs are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages server logging fields autonomous actions retention. Read devtools-addon and view-portal-error-log and PowerPagesLog/WAF-log search excerpts. Existing error diagnostics and WAF schemas do not establish the planned integrated server/access-log schema.

claims.claim: Azure roles control access to Application Insights resources.
claims.quote: Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) provides built-in roles for monitoring to assign to users, groups, service principals, and managed identities. ... View diagnostic settings, autoscale settings, and Application Insights data
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/fundamentals/roles-permissions-security for the Application Insights resource-access statement.

claims.claim: The feature has no autonomous actions and only observes and reports.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages server logging fields autonomous actions retention. Read roadmap, devtools-addon, view-portal-error-log and go-live/telemetry-monitoring; they describe monitoring and debugging, not an exhaustive assurance of no autonomous actions.
claims.fix: Replace 'None. The feature observes and reports.' with 'The roadmap describes telemetry and analytics, not autonomous remediation.'

claims.where: controls[0].governs, scope; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing diagnostic logging sends a selected site's application errors to an Azure Blob storage account.
claims.quote: To access the logs, configure your website to send all application errors to an Azure Blob storage account that you own.

claims.claim: Diagnostic logging is reached in Power Platform admin center through Resources > Power Pages sites > site > Site Actions > Enable diagnostics logs.
claims.quote: Under the Resources section, select Power Pages sites. ... Select your website. ... From the Site Actions menu, select Enable diagnostics logs.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: PAC CLI paragraph
claims.claim: No dedicated API equivalent for enabling Power Pages diagnostic Blob logging is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages diagnostic API enable logging; Power Pages site analytics server logging tenant disable policy diagnostic logging API licensing Application Insights. Read view-portal-error-log, FAQ and PAC CLI documentation; results show UI configuration, not a dedicated enablement API.

claims.claim: The new Power Platform admin center traffic analytics route is Manage > Products > Power Pages > Analytics (preview).
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Manage. ... Under Products, select Power Pages and then select Analytics (preview).

claims.claim: An API equivalent for the site traffic analytics dashboard is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages traffic analytics API. Read admin-center-analytics and go-live/telemetry-monitoring; results describe the dashboard and tracking snippets, not an API equivalent for the dashboard.

claims.claim: The dashboard requires Dynamics 365 administrator, Power Platform administrator, or System administrator, with the last limited to their environments.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 administrator; Power Platform administrator; System administrator (You can only see environments for which you're a system administrator.)

claims.claim: The admin analytics dashboard covers websites across the tenant, filtered by environment and site.
claims.quote: Each chart displays the DAU, WAU, and MAU for all the sites in the selected environment. ... Traffic reports are available only for public sites. Private sites aren't included in these reports.
claims.fix: Replace the dashboard clause with: 'The admin analytics dashboard covers public websites across the tenant, filtered by environment and Site ID; private sites are not included.'

claims.claim: The trace/debug site's settings are reached in the Power Pages Management app through Website > Site settings.
claims.quote: Using the Portal Management app, select Site settings under the Website section. ... To edit an existing setting, select the Site Setting listed in the grid. ... Value: The setting
claims.fix: The route stops on the correct list. Complete it as 'Website > Site settings > UserTrace/Debug > Value' and retain the note about editing the site setting. The cited devtools-addon article specifies UserTrace/Debug and a value of true.

claims.claim: pac pages upload --path <site-folder> --modelVersion <model-version> uploads edited site configuration.
claims.quote: pac pages upload --path "C:\portals\starter-portal" --deploymentProfile "profile-name" --modelVersion 2

claims.claim: UserTrace/Debug is a site setting that enables diagnostic tracing for a public Power Pages site.
claims.quote: To enable the diagnostic setting for a public website: ... Add or update the Site Setting with the name UserTrace/Debug. ... Set the value to true.
